rationale: Round-5 zero-ask regression check of 27294e84 under the grounding lens, with INDEPENDENT empirical verification of every fresh git-mechanics claim in a scratch repo (not trusting the author's re-run lab). LAB RESULTS, all three claims TRUE: (1) `git update-ref --stdin` with start/prepare/commit over two refs (bead ref with expected-old + marker ref) moves BOTH refs atomically on success — verified: main and refs/mindspec/materialized/test both advanced A→C in one transaction. (2) A wrong expected-old on the bead ref aborts WHOLESALE at prepare — verified verbatim: `fatal: prepare: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/main': is at <C> but expected <A>`, exit non-zero, and NEITHER ref moved (the marker update in the same transaction did not apply) — exactly the plan's 'fatal at prepare, neither ref moves' fail-closed semantics, and my test used OLD≠NEW so it does not repeat the author's invalidated first attempt. (3) The S-stage plumbing construction is buildable precisely as described: temp-index `read-tree C` → `hash-object -w` the refreshed artifact → `update-index --cacheinfo` → `write-tree` → `commit-tree <tree> -p C` yields D whose parent is C and whose diff vs C is EXACTLY the artifact path, and the follow-up transaction {bead-ref C→D, marker→D} commits atomically. CONSISTENCY SWEEP: the staged protocol is now stated identically in all three surfaces — the protocol paragraph (M: commit-tree C first, then txn {A→C expected-old, marker→C}; R: idempotent reset; S: D by plumbing + txn {C→D, marker→D}; G: resume routes INTO --resolve-merge; T: terminal clear on both completion paths, with reconcile-detection FIRST in the early sequence), bead 6 step 1 (the transaction helper with wholesale-abort semantics beside the 127 precedents), bead 6 step 4 (the corrected staged order), and the ADR-0041 §1/§3 draft description (full M→R→S→G→T + transactional marker invariant, loose-object qualification preserved). My round-4 minor finding R2-4-2 (marker-before-commit-tree ordering slip) is FIXED — the corrected order 'commit-tree BEFORE any marker can exist' is now explicit in both the protocol paragraph and step 4 (round-4 G1.2). The G2 sweep also verifies: the stale O_EXCL journal-idiom framings are gone from both the lock-home paragraph and bead 1 step 2, replaced consistently by flock/LockFileEx-retained-handle with the journal contributing only the read-modify-write shape. The marker==tip-by-construction invariant now genuinely holds across every tool-authored transition (both transitions are transactional), making marker≠tip a proof of foreignness — the state machine is sound and the three new kill fixtures (ix)/(x)/(xi) pin its edges. ONE minor residual, non-blocking: after the S transaction the real index still sits at C while HEAD is D (delta = the refreshed artifact blob), and the stage list repeats no index refresh after S — so between S and worktree removal, status consumers see the artifact as a staged+unstaged pair. Consequence-free on every current path (the merge runs outside the bead worktree; the worktree is removed on success; resume-from-first-incomplete-stage never consults the bead index; fixture (vi)'s unchanged-artifact scenario never builds D so the fixture is unaffected), but a one-line repetition of the idempotent R refresh after the S transaction would preserve the status-clean invariant the plan otherwise establishes. Recording for fold-in; it does not warrant a round.
